_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: Roof material from evidence, varying per zone
tasks.notes: Cause: feature_build takes one roofs[label].material per label, and the zoned shell uses it for every roof surface (feature_build.py ~916); the designer picked smooth_stone for SUSU, West and Retail with no roof-colour evidence cited in any spec's notes. Covers issue I-010 (every roof in the cell is one block), snag S-015. Scope: optional per-zone roof material override in the spec; the dry run samples the aerial mosaic over each roof zone and prints its mean colour beside the nearest block from the site_kit colour table, as a suggestion for the designer (not a gate). Done when the dry runs of susu_w33830305, west_w34391673 and retail_w33830236 print a roof colour and suggested block per zone, and a spec can give two zones of one building different materials. Check line S-015: roofs differ between buildings, and within a building, where the aerial shows they differ. Not verified: whether these roofs actually differ in colour on the aerial. Touches feature_build.py like #125; work them in sequence or expect a merge. One regression test only; no new gates or lints.

tasks.title: Snap hand-read tree crowns to the lidar canopy
tasks.notes: Cause: in cell 48,-44 the trees come from 58 crowns read by eye from Google z20 crops (world reference/trees-google-crowns.json, 2026-10-16, old Southampton Refine project; trees_layer.google_crowns drops the detector inside its zone, which covers the whole cell). Nothing checks them against lidar. Near snag S-017 the crowns stand on 0-2 m of nDSM while the canopy peaks (8-10 m) lie 4-5 blocks east: (6266,-5572)->(6270,-5575), (6267,-5556)->(6271,-5561), (6265,-5581)->(6270,-5575); two crowns sit about 2 blocks from University Road's centre line. Covers issue I-011 (trees in 48,-44 stand a few blocks off the real trees), snag S-017. Scope: before planting, move each hand-read crown to the highest lidar canopy point (nDSM >= 3 m) within a few blocks (search radius as a named constant); keep a crown in place and print it 'unconfirmed' when no peak is in reach or the peak is on a building footprint. Dry run prints each crown's shift and the share moved. No road rule (owner: fix positions from evidence, not a no-trees-on-roads rule). Done when an offline dry run for 48,-44 moves the three crowns near the snag onto the peaks east of the road and prints shifts for all 58. Check line S-017: the trees along University Road stand on the verge where the real trees are, not on the carriageway. Not verified: that the 8-10 m peaks are trees, not buildings; how the other 55 crowns compare. One regression test only; no new gates or lints.
